title: Update JFR Native Image Support for compatibility with JDK 17

timeline.body: Closes #3538

@christianhaeubl Hi Christian! I started this PR with the intent to let the changes be reviewed sooner rather than later. There is still some work to do for closing chunks properly in 17, but otherwise it compiles and runs without error.

Hello Zhengyu Gu, thanks for contributing a PR to our project!

We use the [Oracle Contributor Agreement](http://www.oracle.com/technetwork/community/oca-486395.html) to make the copyright of contributions clear. We don't have a record of you having signed this yet, based on your email address zgu -(at)- redhat -(dot)- com. You can sign it at that link. 
    
If you think you've already signed it, please comment below and we'll check.

Zhengyu Gu has signed the [Oracle Contributor Agreement](http://www.oracle.com/technetwork/community/oca-486395.html) (based on email address zgu -(at)- redhat -(dot)- com) so can contribute to this repository.

Just noting in a comment here: the current issue is that the jdk.jfr.internal.ShutdownHook to support dumponexit is not running in the image for 17, but is for 11. It's not touched directly by us though, so continuing to investigate.

> Just noting in a comment here: the current issue is that the jdk.jfr.internal.ShutdownHook to support dumponexit is not running in the image for 17, but is for 11. It's not touched directly by us though, so continuing to investigate.

Issue described here is resolved now.
Note this still needs `H:+PlatformInterfaceCompatibilityMode` to compile. Not yet sure how to resolve that.

timeline.body: On older JDK versions, I think that it is still necessary to reset this field.
This substitution should probably be conditional and only be used for JDK versions that do not have the field `JVM.recording` anymore.

So, this is a static field that exists for each event class and that is probably added by instrumentation? Please add some documentation that describes how this works and that this is for certain JDK versions only.

reply.body: Looking at the code path, this should never be reached at runtime since we expect `eventHandler` fields to already be in the image. I've removed this method and altered the substitution to throw an error.

timeline.body: Please update the documentation of the field `private volatile boolean recording;`

reply.body: Sorry, can you clarify what the documentation should be updated with?

Something like:
```
// We need this separate field for all JDK versions, i.e., even for versions where the field JVM.recording is present (JVM.recording is not set for all the cases that we are interested in).
```

timeline.body: What is the reason for copying the `DCmdStart` implementation here? Copying code like that typically creates major issues in the long run.

reply.body:
DCmdStart and surrounding functionality was heavily modified in OpenJDK here: https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/f716711c7b5f442653fcd5402bb9ad9fa8a6501b#diff-437f27c74f0b6eb69196ae8b8a27d398a188da4809c6c755ec8eae771e3f4b94R64

I don't know how to support both method signatures of `DcmdStart.execute` from 11 and 17 so I decided to follow the execution manually instead.

Specifically
```
public String[] execute(String name, String[] settings, Long delay, Long duration, Boolean disk, String path, Long maxAge, Long maxSize, Long flush, Boolean dumpOnExit, Boolean pathToGcRoots) throws DCmdException {
```
to
```
@Override
public void execute(ArgumentParser parser) throws DCmdException {
```

I can revisit this.
If you see any chance of simplifying that, please open a new PR. This PR was merged to master in the meanwhile.

@christianhaeubl Okay. I will create a new issue specifically for DcmdStart support and look at that. Thanks for reviewing and merging this.

I have an attempt similar to HiddenClassSupport but the changes are quite substantial to support the two quite different APIs :|

timeline.body: Does the implementation work with JDK15 and JDK16 as well or is there anything missing for those JDKs?

reply.body: It should be okay for 14+. I wasn't sure which JDK's to care about here. I guess 12/13 don't really exist?

11, 15, 16, and 17 are potentially relevant. Please enable it for those versions if you think that everything works for those version (all your `@TargetElement(onlyWith = ...)` annotations look good).
Okay. I will test those four versions and update `jvmVersionSupported` appropriately.
